record.title: PDE authors prove conditional regularity for an axisymmetric Navier–Stokes blowup profile with analytic forcing
record.summary: Peter Constantin, Mihaela Ignatova and Vlad Vicol report a theorem for suitable weak solutions of forced 3D Navier–Stokes: if the force is bounded in C² up to the proposed singular time and spatially real analytic locally before it, while the angular mean obeys specified anisotropic Type II estimates and the full solution is exactly axisymmetric on a shrinking core at every pre-singular time, then the solution is regular at the point. Their arXiv v2 appendix derives two velocity hypotheses from statements in OpenAI’s proposed construction and conditionally concludes that a force in that construction cannot vanish identically near the singular point or be locally spatially analytic under the stated bound. The paper expressly says it does not verify the OpenAI construction. OpenAI’s described compactly supported smooth residual force is nonanalytic, so the theorem constrains a force class and does not refute the proposed construction or resolve the Clay problem.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: arXiv records v1 submitted 17 Sep 2026 and v2 revised 29 Sep 2026 by Peter Constantin, Mihaela Ignatova and Vlad Vicol.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors claim regularity at the singular point assuming a suitable weak solution, bounded-C² force up to that time, locally uniform spatial analyticity before it, their specified anisotropic Type-II bounds on the angular mean, and exact axisymmetry on a shrinking core at each prior time.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Appendix A.6 conditionally derives force-class consequences for the OpenAI construction from properties the authors attribute to its manuscript, but explicitly does not verify that construction.

claims.label: INFERRED
claims.text: Because the OpenAI manuscript describes its force as compactly supported and smooth, the paper's real-analytic-force hypothesis is not satisfied by that stated force; the conditional theorem does not by itself refute the OpenAI construction.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent PDE-specialist audit of Theorem 1.1 or the derivation in Appendix A.6 was established.
The relation between the conditional regularity theorem and the validity or force behavior of the OpenAI construction remains unsettled; the source authors explicitly do not verify that construction.

brief.importance_rationale: If the conditional theorem and its stated application are correct, it materially narrows the force regularity compatible with a prominent proposed Navier–Stokes blowup profile and informs proof review. Its consequence is notable for PDE and automated-mathematics assessment, but it does not decide the underlying construction or the Millennium problem.
limitations: The authors explicitly say they have not verified correctness of the OpenAI construction; Appendix A.6 derives selected hypotheses from that manuscript.

The theorem requires the conjunction of spatial analyticity and bounded-C² force plus the stated velocity-profile conditions; it does not show every smooth or nonanalytic forcing admits or precludes blowup.

The conditional force-class conclusions rely on the proposed blowup and on the authors' derivation of construction properties; neither this paper nor the research desk's bounded inspection resolves the OpenAI proof.
No independent PDE-specialist review, full proof reproduction, Lean audit, or Clay acceptance/rejection was established.
brief.summary: Peter Constantin, Mihaela Ignatova and Vlad Vicol report a theorem for suitable weak solutions of forced 3D Navier–Stokes: if the force is bounded in C² up to the proposed singular time and spatially real analytic locally before it, while the angular mean obeys specified anisotropic Type II estimates and the full solution is exactly axisymmetric on a shrinking core at every pre-singular time, then the solution is regular at the point. Their arXiv v2 appendix derives two velocity hypotheses from statements in OpenAI’s proposed construction and conditionally concludes that a force in that construction cannot vanish identically near the singular point or be locally spatially analytic under the stated bound. The paper expressly says it does not verify the OpenAI construction. OpenAI’s described compactly supported smooth residual force is nonanalytic, so the theorem constrains a force class and does not refute the proposed construction or resolve the Clay problem.

technical.claimed_result: The authors claim regularity at the putative singular point under the joint hypotheses. They further claim that, conditional on the OpenAI construction's blowup and derived profile properties, its force neither vanishes identically near the singular point nor is locally spatially analytic under the paper's bounded-C² condition.
technical.compute_or_cost: Not applicable; the paper makes no compute-cost claim for the mathematical theorem.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public arXiv v2 text contains Theorem 1.1, its proof, and Appendix A.6 with an explicit conditional application to the OpenAI construction. This establishes what the paper states and how it scopes the application; the research desk has not independently proved the theorem.
technical.implementation_status: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-09-17 and v2 revised 2026-09-29; no independent specialist adjudication or Clay acceptance established in this activation.
technical.mechanism: The authors use anisotropic blowup-scale rescaling and ancient-limit arguments for the vorticity equations, with a comparison principle to show regularity under their joint analytic-force, bounded-C²-force, angular-mean Type-II, and shrinking-core axisymmetry hypotheses.
technical.novelty: The paper gives a concrete regularity theorem under joint assumptions tied to an unusually specific proposed blowup profile, then derives force-class consequences for that profile without claiming to verify the external construction.
technical.regime: Suitable weak solutions of forced incompressible 3D Navier–Stokes on a local cylinder; spatially analytic force on compact pre-singular cylinders, uniformly bounded C² force up to singular time, anisotropic Type-II bounds for the angular mean, and a nonzero exactly axisymmetric core at every pre-singular time.
technical.reproducibility: Full arXiv v2 HTML is accessible and the proof is inspectable, but no independent line-by-line proof audit or specialist reproduction was completed.
technical.strongest_baseline: The source is a theorem paper, not a benchmark. Its relevant comparison is the OpenAI manuscript's own stated construction and force class as cross-referenced in Appendix A.6; the authors explicitly say they do not verify that construction.

brief.title: PDE authors prove conditional regularity for an axisymmetric Navier–Stokes blowup profile with analytic forcing
brief.why_it_matters: If the theorem and its application withstand independent review, it places a precise restriction on the force regularity compatible with a particular high-profile blowup profile and makes part of the proposed construction more inspectable. It sharpens the mathematical regime and review questions around the claim without establishing that the construction is valid or invalid.
